record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant epsilon with 0 < epsilon < 2^(-1/2) such that, whenever f and g belong to L^2_a(D) and |f(z)| <= |g(z)| throughout the annulus epsilon < |z| < 1, it follows that ||f||_L2 <= ||g||_L2?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 8.1 (Korenblum) There exists an absolute constant epsilon

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ such that
$$\|f\|_{L^2}^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon<2^{-1/2}$ such that, for every pair $f,g\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ satisfying
$$|f(z)| \le |g(z)| \quad \text{for all } z \text{ with } \varepsilon < |z| < 1,$$
one has $\|f\|_{L^2} \le \|g\|_{L^2}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Korenblum's maximum principle conjecture for the Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ was proved by W. K. Hayman in 1999, who established the existence of such an absolute constant (with $\varepsilon \approx 1/25$). Hinkkanen subsequently extended the result to $A^p(\mathbb{D})$ for all $p\ge 1$. The sharp value of $\varepsilon$ remains unknown, but the existence question posed here is settled.

status_evidence.title: On a maximum principle in Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Hayman proved Korenblum's conjecture for the Bergman space A^2(D).
status_evidence.claim: Hayman (1999) settled Korenblum's maximum principle conjecture for L^2_a(D).

status_evidence.title: On Korenblum's Maximum Principle
status_evidence.snippet: Hinkkanen extended Hayman's result to A^p for p>=1 with constant 0.15724.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of the absolute constant has been confirmed; sharp value remains open.
